need: My 1 acre tomato is 40 days old. Leaves are curling upward and turning small, and tiny white insects fly up when I touch the plants.
summary: This looks like whitefly-transmitted Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) — a common problem on tomato in India. The plan controls the whitefly vector, protects new seedlings with a net, and offers tolerant seed for replanting if needed; it does not diagnose the virus and the KVK should confirm.
assumptions: Seedlings are in open field, not protected
Whitefly numbers are high based on description
No insecticide has been sprayed yet
expert_questions: Are older leaves also curling, or only new growth?
Are there any mosaic or yellowing patches?
How long ago were the seedlings transplanted?

lines.why: A KVK expert confirms whether it is leaf curl virus before any further spend.
lines.name: KVK / agri-expert field visit voucher

lines.why: Yellow sticky traps monitor and mass-trap the whiteflies that spread the virus — no spraying needed.
lines.name: Yellow sticky traps (pack of 25)

lines.why: A 40-mesh insect-proof net over seedlings is the cheapest way to keep whiteflies off young plants.
lines.name: Insect-proof nursery net, 40 mesh (10 m)

lines.why: Neem oil as a botanical spray reduces sucking pest pressure; it is not a cure for the virus.
lines.name: Neem oil based botanical (azadirachtin, 1 L)

lines.why: ToLCV-tolerant certified seed for replanting if the current crop fails.
lines.name: Certified tomato seed, ToLCV-tolerant hybrid (10 g)

lines.why: Safety kit is mandatory whenever the kit includes something to spray.
lines.name: Spray safety kit: gloves, mask, goggles, apron

notes: Safety floor: spray safety kit added.

need: Rain-fed tur (pigeon pea) on 3 acres in Marathwada, 50 days, no rain for 3 weeks, some yellowing of lower leaves. I also want to store the harvest safely this time.
summary: The yellowing lower leaves in a drought period suggest nitrogen stress compounded by poor soil biology on a rain-fed pulse — a soil test and bio-fertiliser will help. Hermetic storage bags address the post-harvest problem; this is not a diagnosis and the KVK should confirm.
assumptions: Soil has not been tested recently
Rain is unlikely in the next two weeks
Storage problem is from weevils or moisture
expert_questions: Is the yellowing from the bottom upward (nitrogen deficiency) or is it scattered (virus or fungal)?
What was the previous crop on this field?

lines.why: An expert checks whether the yellowing is nitrogen deficiency, drought stress, or a disease before recommending more inputs.
lines.name: KVK / agri-expert field visit voucher

lines.why: A soil test reveals the actual NPK and pH so the next season's fertiliser spend is right.
lines.name: Soil test at an accredited lab (Soil Health Card style: NPK, pH, EC, OC, micronutrients)

lines.why: Rhizobium bio-fertiliser boosts nitrogen fixation in tur and cuts the need for urea next season.
lines.name: Bio-fertiliser trio: Rhizobium/Azotobacter + PSB + KSB (3 x 1 L)

lines.why: A simple rain gauge gives a daily record to decide when supplemental irrigation is really needed.
lines.name: Plastic rain gauge

lines.why: Hermetic bags stop weevils and moisture damage in stored tur grain without any chemicals.
lines.name: Hermetic grain storage bags (pack of 5)

lines.why: A tarpaulin protects the drying grain from unexpected rain during threshing.
lines.name: Tarpaulin sheet 6x8 m (grain drying / rain cover)
